newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures recover late, finish mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures recover late, finish mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures rallied early on bullish data, collapsed later on supply woes, and ended near mid-range on late short-covering.
Traders said the late recovery in March T-bonds back to positive territory was tied to revived hopes for a coupon pass on Wednesday.
One trader called the recovery "a slow grind higher," and noted that late short-covering had become common during T-bond futures' recent rally.
"Just like the past month and a half, we saw some short-covering late in the day," he said.
"We saw some expectations that we could get a coupon pass tomorrow and the bond held losses to the downside," he said.

The midday losses had been sparked by news that IBM had issued $850 million in long-term debt. Long position holders scrambled to get out, pulling the March T-bond from near its 116-17/32 session high to a low of 115-22/32.
Sell-stops below 116-00 in March T-bonds extended the move, traders said.
Traders tied further midday weakness in debt futures to an eroding U.S. dollar.
"You had IBM and the dollar weakness against the yen and no coupon pass, yet we still seem to be holding out hope for a coupon pass tomorrow," another trader said.
"But if we don't get a coupon pass we won't have the short-covering tomorrow," he said.

Early in the day, October single-family home sales were reported down 8.7 percent, launching most contracts to their highs for the day. A drop in BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales index soothed fears about vigorous consumer demand during the Thanksgiving holiday. Chain store sales dropped 0.2 percent in the week ended November 30 from the prior week.
Late in the day, U.S. adjusted retail sales were reported down 0.7 percent in November versus October, according to the Redbook Retail Sales Index.
Just after the open, October leading indicators rose 0.1 percent against an 0.2 percent rise in September.

March T-bond futures settled up 4/32 at 116-00, 10-year T-notes ended 1/32 higher at 111-15/32 and muni-bonds were 7/32 lower at 117-21/32. March IMM T-bills were one basis point higher at 95.05 and Eurodollars were flat at 94.54. ((--Chicago Derivatives desk (312)408-8750)) ((E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
